title: Music Composition and Audio Engineering
answer: Score generation, stem separation, drum programming, mixing and mastering, and generated foley.

children.name: Score Generation and Composition
children.blurb: Score generation and composition covers systems that create musical notation, MIDI, or audio stems for film, game, advertising, and concert work.

children.name: Stem Separation and Restoration
children.blurb: Stem separation and restoration covers isolating individual instrumental or vocal parts from a mixed recording and repairing degraded audio such as noise, clipping, dropouts, or missing spectral content.

children.name: Generative Rhythm and Drum Programming
children.blurb: Generative rhythm and drum programming covers AI systems that create drum patterns, fills, and full percussion arrangements from user inputs such as tempo, genre, feel, or an existing musical phrase.

children.name: Automated Mixing and Mastering
children.blurb: Automated mixing and mastering uses machine learning to set levels, equalization, compression, stereo image, and loudness for recorded music, either as assistive tools or fully autonomous processing.

children.name: Generated Foley and Sound Design
children.blurb: Generated foley and sound design covers AI systems that create or manipulate sound effects, ambiences, footsteps, cloth, impacts, and other non-musical audio for film, television, games, and interactive media.

sections.body: This field covers practical uses of machine learning in music and audio production. Score generation systems now produce full orchestral arrangements, chord progressions, and melodic lines from text prompts or MIDI sketches. Stem separation tools split finished recordings into vocal, drum, bass, and other instrumental parts for remixing or restoration. Drum programming models create rhythm patterns in specific genres, while automated mixing and mastering services adjust levels, equalization, and loudness. Generated foley systems synthesize footsteps, cloth movement, and ambient room tone for film and game audio.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven across these tasks. Stem separation is the most mature, with widely used tools that perform well on clean studio recordings but still struggle with heavily reverberant or overlapping sounds. Score generation can produce convincing short passages, yet long form structure, thematic development, and emotional pacing remain unreliable. Automated mixing and mastering handles basic level balancing and loudness normalization competently, but it does not replace a skilled engineer for complex or unusual material. The site tracks 2000 audio models, and 18 of the 92 active intellectual property lawsuits involve AI music services, which reflects unresolved questions about training data and ownership. Generated foley is useful for background texture but often lacks the precise timing and physical detail of recorded sound.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how systems write melodies and full scores should start with Score Generation and Composition, which covers the models and their musical output. Stem Separation and Restoration explains the tools that isolate or repair individual parts of an existing recording, and it pairs naturally with Automated Mixing and Mastering, where those separated stems might be rebalanced. Generative Rhythm and Drum Programming focuses on beat and percussion pattern creation, a narrower but heavily used area. Generated Foley and Sound Design covers non musical audio for media, from footsteps to environmental noise, and shows how the same underlying audio models are adapted for sound effects.
